questions.q: A regional VPN gateway fails for the fourth time in two months. What should happen, per the capstone mapping?
options: Only log a problem record; don't touch the incident itself
Restore access as an incident right away, and also open a problem record to investigate the recurring root cause
Ignore it since it already resolved itself three times before
Treat it purely as a service request for new hardware
questions.explain: Incident management restores service now; a recurring pattern against the same configuration item is exactly what problem management exists to investigate.

questions.q: An employee requests a new laptop because theirs is being handed down to a new hire. What practice owns this?
options: Problem management, since a laptop is involved
Change enablement, since it changes who has the laptop
Service request management, fulfilled through the Service Catalog
Major incident management
questions.explain: Nothing is broken here — it's a standard, pre-approved fulfillment workflow, not an incident.

questions.q: A security patch needs to go onto the patient-scheduling system during the organization's year-end change freeze. How does change enablement handle this tension?
options: The patch must wait until the freeze ends, no exceptions
The freeze is simply ignored for any change involving security
Through an emergency change path — a faster-moving, still-authorized route for changes that can't wait, even during a freeze
By skipping the CAB for all future changes permanently
questions.explain: An unpatched known vulnerability is itself a risk the freeze was never meant to protect, so emergency change provides an authorized exception path.

questions.q: A new technician keeps escalating simple password resets instead of resolving them at first contact. What does the capstone mapping identify as the real gap?
options: The technician is incompetent and should be replaced
How knowledge is surfaced and onboarded into for new staff, plus whether first-contact resolution is actually measured and reinforced
The service desk needs no process changes at all
This is purely a change enablement issue
questions.explain: If a step-by-step article exists but isn't surfaced to new technicians, the gap is in knowledge management and service desk practice, not the individual.

questions.q: After the change freeze ends, the change manager reviews incident data and spots a disproportionate share of VPN gateway failures. What practice does this represent?
options: IT asset management
Continual improvement — using existing data to find a pattern and plan a fix rather than letting it recur
Service level management only
This isn't related to any ITIL 4 practice
questions.explain: Continual improvement closes the loop by turning a recurring pain point, visible in existing data, into a planned improvement.
